text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Turkey needs a prosecutor with greater powers to investigate the relationship between organised crime, the police and state.
- The main conservative opposition calls for early general elections.
- The inflation rate exceeds 80 percent for the first in the last 17 months.
- Privatisation revenues in 1997 are estimated at $4.1 billion.
- The tourism ministry plans to gather 76 casinos in three regions and permit Turkish citizens to enter the casinos, having earlier banned them from doing so.
- Environmental groups call for the resignation of the environment minister as he plays down the extent of pollution caused by a nuclear power plant in the western city of Izmir.
- The journalist trade union takes a decision for the state-run Anatolian news agency to go on strike.
- The conservative wing of the government agrees on lifting a ban on civil servants wearing Islamist headscarves, as sought by the Islamist partner in the coalition.

- The draft law against money laundering has become a mess before parliament debates it. A delay in passing it will cause Ankara a headache as there is international concern about money laundering in Turkey.
